title_en: The Establishment of the Month of Ramadan
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين.

أما بعد فإن أهل العلم اختلفوا في ثبوت الأهلة هل هو من باب الشهادة أو من باب الرواية، فذهب مالك رحمه الله وكذلك أبو حنيفة إلى أن ثبوت الأهلة إنما هو من باب الشهادة لما يترتب عليه من الحقوق الخاصة، كآجال الديون وكعدد النساء ونحو ذلك، والفرق بين باب الرواية وباب الشهادة أن باب الشهادة يتعلق به الحقوق الخاصة، وباب الرواية إنما يتعلق به الحقوق العامة التي لا مرافعة فيها ولا منازعة..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon the one who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his practice until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: the people of knowledge differed over the establishment of the new moons — whether it falls under the heading of testimony (shahādah) or under the heading of transmission (riwāyah). Malik, God have mercy on him, and likewise Abu Hanifa, held that the establishment of the new moons falls under the heading of testimony, because of the particular rights that follow from it, such as the terms of debts and the waiting periods of women (ʿiddah) and the like. The difference between the heading of transmission and the heading of testimony is that particular rights attach to the heading of testimony, whereas only general rights attach to the heading of transmission — rights in which there is no pleading and no dispute..

flags.arabic: فإن أهل العلم اختلفوا في ثبوت الأهلة … لا مرافعة فيها ولا منازعة..
flags.context: the whole of the published excerpt
options: render faithfully, mark as an excerpt, and suppress or caveat it as a fatwa
render and present as the Sheikh's position on sighting the new moon
render and present the reported position as the settled ruling
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY — STYLE GUIDE §10. This excerpt sets out a disagreement among jurists and breaks off, on a double full stop, before the Sheikh gives any position of his own. The last position stated is that of Malik and Abu Hanifa, and a reader will inevitably take it for his fatwa on how Ramadan is established. It is not: it is a reported position inside an argument whose conclusion is in the .docx download. This must not be rendered as a fatwa; the site should suppress it or carry a prominent caveat.

flags.arabic: ثبوت الأهلة … من باب الشهادة أو من باب الرواية
flags.context: the question the lecture opens on
options: under the heading of testimony (shahādah) or of transmission (riwāyah)
a matter of witness evidence or of report
a question of legal testimony or of hadith narration
flags.note: bāb here is the technical 'chapter/heading' under which a question is classified, and the whole argument turns on which chapter the sighting of the new moon belongs to, because the evidentiary standards differ. Option 2 loses the classification and reads as an ordinary contrast; option 3 over-specifies riwāyah as hadith narration, which is narrower than the Sheikh's use. A reviewer should confirm the rendering, as these two terms will recur across the corpus.

flags.context: the examples of particular rights that follow from establishing the new moon
flags.note: ʿidad here is the plural of ʿiddah, the waiting period, not ʿadad, 'number'. The source is unvowelled and the wrong reading produces nonsense in English, so the reading is recorded.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-21 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer or delivered the lecture. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
The opening is the khuṭbat al-ḥājah, the standard formula with which the Sheikh begins a lecture. It is rendered in full rather than abbreviated, since it is part of the text as published.

EXCERPT ONLY. The page publishes the opening of the lecture and breaks off; the full text sits behind the .docx download recorded in source_download_link. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and the thought has not been completed. The site must render this with an excerpt banner and never as a whole article.
The positions of Malik and Abu Hanifa are reported positions and the English keeps them explicitly attributed. The Sheikh states no position of his own anywhere in the published text.
The excerpt ends on a double full stop in the source, which appears to mark the break rather than to be punctuation; it is preserved in body_ar and rendered as-is at the end of body_en.
The title names Ramadan, but the text as published discusses the establishment of the new moons generally and never reaches Ramadan specifically.
